Cargo

Acolchoamento de tanque

Process of introducing inert gas (often nitrogen) into the tank vapor space to maintain safe conditions, prevent air ingress, and control tank atmosphere.

Questions and answers

Questions and answers

What is Acolchoamento de tanque?

In this glossary, Acolchoamento de tanque refers to: Process of introducing inert gas (often nitrogen) into the tank vapor space to maintain safe conditions, prevent air ingress, and control tank atmosphere.

How is Acolchoamento de tanque used in maritime?

In maritime communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "Terminal para navio: Inicie o acolchoamento do tanque com nitrogênio antes da transferência de carga."

Why does Acolchoamento de tanque matter in maritime?

Acolchoamento de tanque matters because it supports clear communication in Cargo contexts for Deck Officers, Engine Officers, and Masters. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as STCW, Marlins Test, ISF Watchkeeper, and GMDSS.

Who uses Acolchoamento de tanque?

Acolchoamento de tanque is mainly used by Deck Officers, Engine Officers, and Masters.

What category does Acolchoamento de tanque belong to?

In this glossary, Acolchoamento de tanque is grouped under Cargo. Related pages in this category explain adjacent procedures, commands and operational concepts.

Where does this definition come from?

This definition is sourced from IMO SMCP, STCW Convention, SOLAS, COLREG and published by Protermify Maritime as a static maritime reference page.

Definition

Process of introducing inert gas (often nitrogen) into the tank vapor space to maintain safe conditions, prevent air ingress, and control tank atmosphere.

Operational example

Terminal to vessel: Initiate tank padding with nitrogen before starting cargo transfer to maintain an inert atmosphere.

Localized term

Acolchoamento de tanque

Localized example

Terminal para navio: Inicie o acolchoamento do tanque com nitrogênio antes da transferência de carga.
